Cookies and measurement

This site uses one third-party tool: Google's measurement (Google Ireland Ltd, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland). It tells us whether our Google ads bring in calls, and which pages get read.

Only the Google Ads script loads as soon as you open the page, before you choose. Until you accept, and also if you refuse, it doesn't set or read any cookie. When the page opens, it sends Google, without a cookie: the time, the page address and the one you came from, whether that address carried an ad-click code (the code itself is replaced by a 0), whether you accepted or not, a random number for that page load, and a few technical settings of the tag. If you tap a call or WhatsApp button, it also sends, without a cookie, to count the call: the page title, the screen size, your device model, its system, the browser and their versions. As with any connection, Google also sees your IP address and browser type. No identifier is kept from one page to the next. Audience measurement (Google Analytics) only loads if you accept it. If you accept, Google may set cookies for ad measurement and for audience measurement, for the lifetimes in the table below.

A banner offers "Refuse all" and "Accept all", equally visible and equally simple, plus a "Choose" button that lets you accept one measurement and refuse the other. Both switches are off until you turn them on yourself. We run no personalised advertising and no retargeting: ad personalisation stays denied even if you accept everything.

For the cookies, the legal basis is your consent. You can withdraw it whenever you want, with the "Cookies and measurement" link at the bottom of every page: exactly as easy as giving it. Refusing deletes the cookies concerned. The ad measurement without cookies rests on our legitimate interest: knowing whether our Google ads bring in calls.

What lands on your device

Here is exactly what lands on your device if you accept, and what stays even if you refuse.

pd_consent is not a cookie, it is a small note your browser keeps. It remembers your answer so we do not ask again on every page. It stays 182 days, then the question comes back. It goes nowhere and holds nothing but your choice. Google's lifetimes are the ones Google publishes and can change, which is why they say "up to".

The site's call counter

If you accept ad measurement and you came from a Google ad, a Google tool may swap the number we show for a Google forwarding number. Your call then goes through Google and still reaches us as usual. That's how we know which ads bring in calls. Google then shows us, in our Google Ads account: the time of the call, how long it lasted, whether it was answered or missed, the caller's country and area code and, for most calls over 15 seconds, your phone number. This tool may set a cookie, gwcc. Without your yes to ad measurement, this tool doesn't load and you always see our real number.

Outside the European Union

Google may process the measurement data outside the European Union, including in the United States. Google does so under the European adequacy decision for the United States and its standard contractual clauses. Your IP address: until you accept ad measurement, Google Ads truncates it (cuts part of it off) as soon as it arrives. If you accept, Google Ads gets it in full. Google Analytics only loads if you accept it. It then handles European visitors' IP addresses on European servers, uses them only to work out your location, and deletes them straight away without storing them.

The fonts and the photos stay on our own server. When you open this page, your browser contacts only one other company: Google, for the measurement described above.

There is one exception, and it does not come from us: our host, Cloudflare Pages, adds two technical headers of its own to every page (NEL and Report-To), and we cannot remove them. They only serve to report a technical error if a page fails to load. In that case the browser sends a technical report to Cloudflare. In our testing, no such report was ever sent.

Our host keeps technical logs (IP address, date, page requested, browser type) for the security and the proper working of the site. These logs are kept briefly and are not used to profile you.

The data you give us yourself

There is no form on this site. You contact us by phone, by WhatsApp or by e-mail. In that case we handle:

  • your name, your phone number and, if you give it, your e-mail;
  • the address of the job;
  • the description of the problem, and the photos or videos you send us;
  • the data needed for the invoice and the payment.

Why, and on what basis

  • Giving you a price and coming to your door: performance of the contract, or steps taken before it.
  • Invoicing and accounting: legal obligation.
  • A report for your insurance, if you ask for one: performance of the contract.
  • Job photos published on this site: only with your agreement, without your name and without your address. At most we name the town and the month. You can withdraw your agreement at any time.
  • Knowing whether our ads bring in calls, with Google's cookies and call counter: your consent, which you can withdraw whenever you want.
  • The ad measurement without cookies, before you choose or if you refuse: our legitimate interest in knowing whether our ads bring in calls.

Who receives your data

Our technician, to come to your door. Our accountant and the tax administration, for the invoices. Our host, to keep the site running. The provider of our e-mail box. WhatsApp (Meta) if you choose that channel yourself. Google Ireland Ltd, for the measurement described above (Google Ads, with no cookies until you accept, and Google Analytics, only if you accept it), and only for that measurement. We sell no data and we send no advertising.

How long

Invoices and accounting documents: ten years, as Belgian law requires. Messages and photos linked to a job: two years after the job, unless a dispute is running. Enquiries with no follow-up: six months.

Your rights

You can ask for access to your data, for it to be corrected or erased, for the processing to be limited, for portability, and you can object to a processing. Write to info@prodebouchage24.be or call 0480 649 649. We answer within the month.

If our answer does not satisfy you, you can lodge a complaint with the Data Protection Authority, rue de la Presse 35, 1000 Brussels, www.dataprotectionauthority.be.
